cumleler: How fast do your eyes respond when you turn your head?
The vestibulo-ocular reflex, or VOR, keeps the image steady on the retina.
The eye response starts less than ten milliseconds after head movement.
Visual tracking systems work with a delay of about one hundred milliseconds.
So when running or turning quickly, the VOR keeps our vision clear.
This speed comes from a short, three-neuron reflex arc.
